Archive item 1: Registration and By-laws of Sunrise Residency Apartment Owners Association
Source format: Association registration and by-laws

1.3 Legal Status: The Sunrise Residency Apartment Owners Association is registered under the Karnataka Apartment Owners Act, 1972, with Registration No. SRA/BLR/2010/1147. The Association is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. The Association may sue and be sued in its own name.

1.4 Amendments: These By-laws may be amended only by a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of the total number of members present and voting at a duly convened general body meeting. All amendments shall be recorded and filed with the registering authority within thirty days of their adoption.

---

ARTICLE II: MEMBERSHIP

2.1 Eligibility: Membership of the Association shall be open to all persons who hold a deed of apartment in the Sunrise Residency complex, as defined under Section 2(a) of the Karnataka Apartment Owners Act, 1972. Each apartment owner shall be entitled to one membership, irrespective of the number of apartments owned by that person.

2.2 Joint Ownership: In the case of joint ownership, the co-owners shall nominate one of themselves as the voting member. Such nomination shall be made in writing and lodged with the Secretary of the Association. The nomination may be changed at any time by a written request signed by all co-owners.

2.3 Nominees and Legal Representatives: In the event of the death of a member, the legal heirs or nominees shall be entitled to membership upon production of appropriate legal documents, including but not limited to a succession certificate, probate of will, or letters of administration.

2.4 Transfer of Membership: Membership shall be transferable only with the transfer of the deed of apartment. The transferee shall become a member upon intimation to the Secretary and upon payment of a transfer fee of ₹500 (Rupees Five Hundred only).

2.5 Cessation of Membership: A person shall cease to be a member upon:
(a) Transfer of ownership of the apartment;
(b) Death, subject to the provisions of Clause 2.3 above;
(c) Expulsion by a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of the members present and voting at a general body meeting, provided that the member has been given a reasonable opportunity to be heard.

The Sunrise Residency Apartment Owners Association is registered under the Karnataka Apartment Owners Act, 1972. Record status: current.

2.6 Register of Members: The Association shall maintain a Register of Members containing the name, address, contact number, email address, and the apartment number of each member. The Register shall be open for inspection by any member during reasonable working hours upon prior appointment.

---

ARTICLE III: OBJECTS AND POWERS OF THE ASSOCIATION

3.1 Objects: The objects of the Association shall be:
(a) To manage, maintain, and repair the common areas and facilities of Sunrise Residency;
(b) To collect maintenance charges and other levies from members;
(c) To enforce the observance of these By-laws and the rules and regulations of the complex;
(d) To take all necessary steps for the preservation of the property and the welfare of the residents;
(e) To engage and supervise staff for the maintenance and security of the complex;
(f) To enter into contracts and agreements for the provision of services to the complex;
(g) To do all such other acts and things as may be necessary or incidental to the above objects.

3.2 Powers: Subject to the provisions of the Karnataka Apartment Owners Act, 1972, and these By-laws, the Association shall have the power to:
(a) Acquire, hold, and dispose of movable and immovable property;
(b) Open and operate bank accounts;
(c) Borrow money for the purposes of the Association, with the prior approval of the general body;
(d) Appoint and remove employees and contractors;
(e) Institute and defend legal proceedings in the name of the Association.

---

ARTICLE IV: OFFICE BEARERS AND THEIR ROLES

4.1 Composition: The Executive Committee (hereinafter referred to as "the Committee") shall consist of the following office bearers and members:
(a) President
(b) Vice-President
(c) Secretary
(d) Joint Secretary
(e) Treasurer
(f) Three Executive Members
ARTICLE IV (continued)

4.2 Tenure: The office bearers and Executive Members shall hold office for a term of two years from the date of election, or until their successors are duly elected and installed, whichever is later. No office bearer shall hold the same post for more than two consecutive terms. A break of one full term shall be required before a person can again contest for the same post.

4.3 Duties of the President: The President shall preside over all meetings of the Association and of the Executive Committee. She/he shall supervise the working of the Committee, sign all agreements and contracts on behalf of the Association, and jointly operate the bank accounts with the Treasurer or Secretary. The President shall have a casting vote in the event of a tie at any meeting of the Committee.

4.4 Duties of the Vice-President: The Vice-President shall assist the President and perform the duties of the President in her/his absence. In the event of a vacancy in the office of the President, the Vice-President shall hold charge until a new President is elected at a special general body meeting.

4.5 Duties of the Secretary: The Secretary shall be responsible for the day-to-day administration of the Association, issue notices for all meetings, maintain the minutes book, attend to all correspondence, and keep the Register of Members up to date. The Secretary shall also maintain custody of the common seal of the Association, if any, and all records other than the financial records.

4.6 Duties of the Joint Secretary: The Joint Secretary shall assist the Secretary and perform the duties of the Secretary in her/his absence. The Joint Secretary shall also maintain a record of all assets of the Association, including furniture, equipment, and other movable property belonging to the Association.

4.7 Duties of the Treasurer: The Treasurer shall have custody of all funds of the Association, maintain proper books of account, receive all moneys on behalf of the Association and issue receipts, and make payments as authorised by the Committee. The Treasurer shall present a statement of income and expenditure at each meeting of the Committee and a full audited statement at the annual general meeting. All cheques and withdrawal forms shall be signed jointly by any two of the following: Treasurer, Secretary, and President.

4.8 Duties of Executive Members: The Executive Members shall attend all meetings of the Committee, participate in the deliberations, and carry out such duties as may be assigned to them by the Committee from time to time. They shall also act as convenors of sub-committees formed for specific purposes such as festival celebrations, security, or repairs.

4.9 Resignation: Any office bearer or Executive Member may resign by submitting a written resignation to the Secretary. Such resignation shall take effect from the date of its acceptance by the Committee or from the date specified in the resignation letter, whichever is later. In the case of resignation by the Secretary, the resignation shall be submitted to the President.

4.10 Removal: A member of the Committee may be removed from office by a resolution passed by a simple majority of the members present and voting at a special general body meeting called for this purpose. The grounds for removal shall be: (a) failure to attend three consecutive meetings of the Committee without sufficient cause; (b) misappropriation of Association funds; (c) acting in a manner detrimental to the interests of the Association; or (d) conviction of an offence involving moral turpitude. The member concerned shall be given an opportunity to present her/his case before the general body prior to any vote on removal.

4.11 Vacancies: Any vacancy arising in the Committee due to resignation, removal, death, or otherwise shall be filled by the Committee by co-option of a member of the Association, subject to the approval of the next general body meeting. A person co-opted to fill a vacancy shall hold office for the remainder of the term of the member whose place she/he has taken.

ARTICLE IV (continued)

4.2 Tenure: The office bearers and Executive Members shall hold office for a term of two years from the date of election, or until their successors are duly elected and installed, whichever is later. No office bearer shall hold the same post for more than two consecutive terms. A break of one full term shall be required before a person can again contest for the same post.

4.3 Duties of the President: The President shall preside over all meetings of the Association and of the Executive Committee. She/he shall supervise the working of the Committee, sign all agreements and contracts on behalf of the Association, and jointly operate the bank accounts with the Treasurer or Secretary. The President shall have a casting vote in the event of a tie at any meeting of the Committee.

4.4 Duties of the Vice-President: The Vice-President shall assist the President and perform the duties of the President in her/his absence. In the event of a vacancy in the office of the President, the Vice-President shall hold charge until a new President is elected at a special general body meeting.

4.5 Duties of the Secretary: The Secretary shall be responsible for the day-to-day administration of the Association, issue notices for all meetings, maintain the minutes book, attend to all correspondence, and keep the Register of Members up to date. The Secretary shall also maintain custody of the common seal of the Association, if any, and all records other than the financial records.

4.6 Duties of the Joint Secretary: The Joint Secretary shall assist the Secretary and perform the duties of the Secretary in her/his absence. The Joint Secretary shall also maintain a record of all assets of the Association, including furniture, equipment, and other movable property belonging to the Association.

4.7 Duties of the Treasurer: The Treasurer shall have custody of all funds of the Association, maintain proper books of account, receive all moneys on behalf of the Association and issue receipts, and make payments as authorised by the Committee. The Treasurer shall present a statement of income and expenditure at each meeting of the Committee and a full audited statement at the annual general meeting. All cheques and withdrawal forms shall be signed jointly by any two of the following: Treasurer, Secretary, and President.

4.8 Duties of Executive Members: The Executive Members shall attend all meetings of the Committee, participate in the deliberations, and carry out such duties as may be assigned to them by the Committee from time to time. They shall also act as convenors of sub-committees formed for specific purposes such as festival celebrations, security, or repairs.

4.9 Resignation: Any office bearer or Executive Member may resign by submitting a written resignation to the Secretary. Such resignation shall take effect from the date of its acceptance by the Committee or from the date specified in the resignation letter, whichever is later. In the case of resignation by the Secretary, the resignation shall be submitted to the President.

4.10 Removal: A member of the Committee may be removed from office by a resolution passed by a simple majority of the members present and voting at a special general body meeting called for this purpose. The grounds for removal shall be: (a) failure to attend three consecutive meetings of the Committee without sufficient cause; (b) misappropriation of Association funds; (c) acting in a manner detrimental to the interests of the Association; or (d) conviction of an offence involving moral turpitude. The member concerned shall be given an opportunity to present her/his case before the general body prior to any vote on removal.

4.11 Vacancies: Any vacancy arising in the Committee due to resignation, removal, death, or otherwise shall be filled by the Committee by co-option of a member of the Association, subject to the approval of the next general body meeting. A person co-opted to fill a vacancy shall hold office for the remainder of the term of the member whose place she/he has taken.

e) **Request for CCTV camera in service elevator:** Mr. Imran Khan raised the issue that the service elevator near the garbage chute does not have CCTV coverage. f) **Clarification on maintenance fee due date:** Several members asked for clarification regarding the due date for the monthly maintenance fee. **6. Proposal for Rainwater Harvesting Project**

The President informed the members that the association has been considering a rainwater harvesting project to improve groundwater recharge and to reduce the dependence on water tankers during the summer months. He stated that the borewell levels in the complex have been depleting over the past two years, and the present system of rainwater drainage does not allow for any collection or recharge.

The President presented the broad outline of the proposed project, which includes the following components:

- Construction of recharge pits at three identified locations within the complex
- Installation of a filtration system to remove debris before the water enters the recharge pits
- Laying of additional piping to connect the terrace drain outlets to the recharge pits
- Minor civil works for the pits and the connecting channels

Sunrise Residency Apartment Owners Association proposed rainwater harvesting project cost is 500000 INR. Record status: pending verification.

The Treasurer, Mrs. Lakshmi Venkatesh, noted that the amount of ₹5,00,000 is a substantial outlay and will require careful consideration. She informed the members that the current balance in the common fund is approximately ₹3,40,000, and the pending maintenance collections amount to about ₹1,80,000. She stated that if the project is approved, the amount could be met from these funds, but it would leave the association with a very thin buffer for any emergency repairs. She suggested that the project could be phased, with the first phase comprising the recharge pits and the second phase taking up the piping work.

A detailed discussion followed. Some members expressed support for the project, noting that the complex spends nearly ₹1,50,000 per year on water tankers during the summer. Others raised concerns about the adequacy of the proposed design, particularly whether the recharge pits would be able to handle the volume of water during heavy rains. Mr. Prakash Gowda, who has some experience in civil works, suggested that the association could obtain a second opinion from a civil engineer before committing to the project.

The President clarified that the project has not yet been approved and is only at the proposal stage. He stated that the details of the design, the phasing, and the exact scope of work will be examined by a small sub-committee, and a firm proposal with a detailed cost breakup will be presented at the next General Body Meeting. The members will be given at least two weeks' notice before the GBM so that they can study the proposal and provide their inputs.

**Status: Proposal only – not yet approved. No financial commitment has been made. The proposal will be tabled at the next GBM for discussion and voting.**
